title: BatchEnsemble rank-one Mirror ensemble
hypothesis: A small structured orthogonal Mirror modulation bank applied to shared hidden weights yields higher ensemble quality-per-byte than native BatchEnsemble rank-one factors at equal member count.
controls: Givens rotation plus member-specific phase Mirror
independent four-member upper control (declared infeasible in this minimal harness)

development.allowed: fixed 500 optimizer updates and lr 0.003; no fresh access until development summary frozen

storage.authority: actual torch.save payload bytes including full state_dict and metadata

success_gate: At equal-or-lower serialized bytes than BatchEnsemble, Mirror improves ensemble mean accuracy by >=2 percentage points or reduces NLL >=5% in every fresh world; ECE regression <=0.02.
failure_gate: Mirror fails both accuracy and NLL gates across fresh worlds or has no member diversity beyond the shared model.
boundaries: Synthetic task only; no natural-data or broad calibration claims.
Four outputs from the same trained shared model are not independent ensemble members; interpretation is a view-quality screen.
Actual deployment comparison charges the entire serialized model state for every method.
